title: Find Indices With Index and Value Difference I
statement:
Given an integer array `nums` of length `n` and two integers `indexDifference` and `valueDifference`, look for a pair of indices `i` and `j` (each from `0` to `n - 1`, and they are allowed to be the same index) such that:

- `abs(i - j) >= indexDifference`
- `abs(nums[i] - nums[j]) >= valueDifference`

Return `[i, j]` for any such pair; when several pairs qualify, any one of them is accepted. If no pair qualifies, return `[-1, -1]`.
signature: int[] findIndices(int[] nums, int indexDifference, int valueDifference)
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 100 numbers there are only about 10,000 index pairs, so checking them is cheap. The pair order does not matter for either condition (both use absolute differences), so it is enough to look at pairs with `i <= j`. The index rule then says `j` must be at least `i + indexDifference`, so the inner loop can start right there and never test a pair that is too close.

## Approach

1. Let `i` run over every index.
2. Start `j` at `i + indexDifference`; every `j` from there to the end is far enough from `i`.
3. If `abs(nums[i] - nums[j]) >= valueDifference`, return `[i, j]` at once, since any valid pair is accepted.
4. If the loops end without a match, return `[-1, -1]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [5, 1, 4, 1]`, `indexDifference = 2`, `valueDifference = 4`. With `i = 0`, `j` starts at `2`: `abs(5 - 4) = 1` is too small. Then `j = 3`: `abs(5 - 1) = 4` is enough, so the answer is `[0, 3]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): at most one check per pair `i <= j`.
- Space: O(1): only the loop indices.

## Pitfalls

- `i` and `j` may be equal: with `indexDifference = 0` and `valueDifference = 0`, `[0, 0]` is already valid.
- When `indexDifference` is at least `n`, no pair is far enough apart; the inner loop simply never runs.
- Use the absolute value of the difference; `nums[j]` may be smaller than `nums[i]`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `i` | the first index, the smaller of the two |
| `j` | the second index, at least `indexDifference` after `i` |

narration.4: Start j at the closest position that is far enough from i, and scan to the end.
narration.5: Are the two values at least valueDifference apart?
